newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks sink at close on bluechip selling.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks sink at close on bluechip selling.

text.p: Sales of blue chip stocks by foreigners during Thursday's morning session triggered forced selling orders by retail cients and sent the battered Thai market to a new year low Wednesday, analysts said.
The SET Index closed at a new year low of 832.60, down 21.22 points or 2.49 percent. The SET 50 closed at 62.55 down 1.92 points or 2.93 percent on trade worth 4.2 billion.
"With the SET going down it forced sales, there were no new numbers or factors in the afternoon," said an analyst at Sitca Investment and Securities.

Thai blue chips, particularly bank stocks, took a heavy battering after Krung Thai Bank's failed attempts to cut annual bonus payments to help meet loan loss provisions was interpreted as a sign of deteriorating portfolio quality.

Investors transmitted those concerns to other bank stocks during the morning session, brokers said. The falling market saw brokers force retail clients to sell stocks which sent the finance sector down 5.5 percent.
